title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tuvalu: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tuvalu: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Tuvalu: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Preparing healthcare, workplace leave, provident fund, civil status, and estate records in advance in Tuvalu gives families clear instructions suited to island hospital and land-tenure realities. Because domestic ministry websites offer minimal online administrative guidance, this planning guide draws directly on verified Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF) statutory rules, Tuvalu statutory texts, and accredited regional diplomatic guidance [1][4][6][8][9][11].

steps.title: Hospital care coordination, infrastructure limits, and statutory leave
steps.html:
• Coordinate medical care, specialist assessments, and medical travel planning with Princess Margaret Hospital in Funafuti (+688 20765; emergency dispatch 911) [9][10]. Discuss treatment and end-of-life preferences early with the attending clinician, noting diplomatic reports that local hospital refrigeration capacity is limited, cremation is unavailable, and international medical evacuation or overseas transport requires advance commercial arrangements [9].
  • Check statutory leave under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2017 (in force since October 2018), which provides employees with at least 5 days of paid sick leave per completed year of continuous service paid at normal wages [7]. Public servants should also verify public-service medical leave and compassionate allowances with their ministry HR desk [7].
  • Note early if landowner consent will later be required for family land burial, because Tuvalu has no designated public cemetery [9].

steps.title: Estate planning, Lands Court vs. High Court rules, and proxy clarity
steps.html:
• Prepare or review a written Will addressing non-customary bank accounts, vehicles, and personal property for High Court jurisdiction, while addressing customary land and native property separately in accordance with the Native Lands Act and island Lands Court practice [1][6].
  • Confirm statutory or legal filing questions through Office of the Attorney General (+688 20823) or qualified legal counsel in Funafuti [6][9].
  • Clarify financial and care decision-making in advance: because Tuvalu lacks an automated public advance-directive portal, communicate treatment wishes directly with Princess Margaret Hospital clinicians while capacity is clear and verify bank signatory or Power of Attorney rules early [9].

steps.title: Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF) nominations and Incapacity Benefit
steps.html:
• Review and update beneficiary nomination forms in person with Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF) (P.O. Box 51, Vaiaku, Funafuti; +688 20983 / +688 20693 / +688 20698; Monday to Friday 9:00 AM to 1:30 PM) or through outer-island Kaupule representatives [2][3][4]. Keeping a valid TNPF nomination is critical because missing or invalid nominations divert distribution to the Lands Department and Lands Court under the TNPF Act [1].
  • Where sickness or injury leaves a contributing member partially or totally incapacitated and unable to work in any occupation for income or gain, review TNPF Incapacity Benefit eligibility: qualified applicants receive a lump sum equal to total accumulated savings (member, employer, and voluntary contributions plus earned interest) upon submitting the Incapacity Application Form, a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner, TNPF ID Card, and bank account details [2][5].
  • Also note the AUD$ 20 application fee required for future Death Benefit applications under TNPF procedures [1].

steps.title: Vital status alignment, tax position, and safe custody
steps.html:
• Verify spelling consistency across birth certificates, marriage certificates, passports, and TNPF membership cards against entries held by Birth Registry Office (Funafuti) (or outer-island Kaupule registries) under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act (Cap. 17.10) [6][8][11].
  • Confirm personal income tax or business tax compliance with domestic tax officers; Tuvalu does not impose a separate inheritance or estate tax [11].
  • Keep original signed Wills, TNPF statements, bank passbooks, and land ownership records stored cleanly in a waterproof folder known to trusted family members [1][2].

steps.title: Cross-border legalisation readiness and family inventory
steps.html:
• Because Tuvalu is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, certified vital certificates and court records sent to foreign banks, insurers, or overseas registries require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than an Apostille [12].
  • Compile a clear written household inventory listing TNPF membership numbers, Birth Registry details, local and overseas bank accounts, employer HR contacts, and Kaupule or Lands Court references [1][3][11].
  • Confirm accredited consular contacts (such as regional embassy contacts covering Tuvalu from Suva) early when family members live overseas [9][10].

contacts.name: Princess Margaret Hospital
contacts.note: Primary hospital in Funafuti providing clinical care, medical certificates, and referrals; national emergency line 911.

contacts.name: Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF)
contacts.note: Vaiaku, Funafuti (P.O. Box 51; +688 20983 / 20693 / 20698) plus outer-island Kaupule hours; handles Incapacity Benefits and member nominations.

contacts.name: Birth Registry Office (Funafuti)
contacts.note: Central registry in Funafuti maintaining vital records alongside outer-island Local Government Councils (Kaupule).

contacts.name: Office of the Attorney General
contacts.note: Central legal oversight office in Funafuti (+688 20823).
